notes:
These are notes on Acts 4, based on the pages I was able to read. Some sources are missing. I ran out of searches before reaching any Catholic or Orthodox site (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org), bibleodyssey.org, the NET Bible notes themselves, or any prosperity or word-of-faith material. I also only saw David Guzik's page up to v. 21; later points from him come from search snippets. Verses with nothing found are left out.

---

## Part 1: The traditional reading, verse by verse

**v. 1** The "captain of the temple" was the head of the temple police. Boice says the original wording suggests they grabbed Peter and John suddenly. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Sources disagree about who the captain was. Matthew Henry says he is thought to have been a Roman officer in charge of the garrison guarding the temple, so Jews and Gentiles were again joined against Christ. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm
- Precept Austin, citing Vincent, says instead that Levites guarded the temple gates under an official Jewish writings called "the man of the Temple Mount." https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Wesley sees God's wisdom here: the apostles spoke first in the temple and then before the council, which they could never have reached unless brought in as criminals. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/acts-4.html

**v. 2** The Sadducees were especially upset because they flatly rejected the resurrection, which is exactly what Peter and John were preaching. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Precept Austin, citing MacArthur, adds that the Sadducees also rejected predestination and God's sovereignty, and calls them the first persecutors of the church. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Henry says the leaders were upset both that the gospel was preached so openly and that the people were so eager to hear it. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**v. 3** Guzik notes the rough arrest. Because v. 21 speaks of "further" threats, he concludes they had already been threatened. The whole setting was meant to frighten them. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/

**v. 4** The two sources read the number differently.
- Guzik takes it as growth from the 3,000 of Acts 2:41 to 5,000. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Henry takes the 5,000 as additional to the 3,000 mentioned earlier, and notes the church's times of suffering have often been its times of growth. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm
- Albert Barnes (via Precept Austin) says persecuting people tends to strengthen them in their beliefs and spread those beliefs. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary

**vv. 5–6** Wesley says the rulers, elders and scribes were known for power, wisdom, and learning. He also notes that Annas had been high priest and Caiaphas was high priest at the time. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/
- Guzik points out this was the same court that had just condemned Jesus, and it meant to show its power. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Homer Kent (via Precept Austin) says the court was acting within its rights. Deuteronomy 13:1-5 required that anyone who used a miracle as the basis for teaching be examined. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary

**v. 7** Guzik says "power" and "name" mean nearly the same thing here, since a name stood for the person's character. He thinks the question itself was fair, but the pressure behind it was not. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Wesley reads it as "by what authority," and thinks they spoke vaguely on purpose. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/
- Henry notes it is the same question they had put to Jesus (Matthew 21:23). https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**v. 8** Guzik says the filling of Acts 2:4 was not a one-time event. Peter's boldness was the evidence of a fresh filling. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Wesley says Peter was filled "that moment," because God moves His instruments when He sees it is needed, not when they please. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/
- Precept Austin says Peter didn't get more of the Spirit; the Spirit got more of him. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary

**v. 9** Guzik: Peter's point was simple. Why are we on trial for a good deed? His tone shows he was not intimidated. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/

**v. 10** Wesley notes the leaders had paid the soldiers to spread a false story about the empty tomb, yet did not dare raise it in front of Peter and John. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/acts-4.html
- Henry: Peter presents the resurrection as the strongest evidence for Jesus and against his persecutors. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**v. 11** Guzik: Psalm 118:22 fits because Jesus, rejected by these very leaders, was raised up by his Father. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Precept Austin notes Peter adds "by you" to the quotation, aiming it at the court itself. It also says Peter chose a stronger word for "rejected" than the Greek Old Testament uses, one that also means despised. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary

**v. 12** Guzik: Peter presents Jesus not as a way of salvation but as the only way. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Henry: we are lost unless we take shelter in this name. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**v. 13** Guzik: "unschooled" means without formal rabbinic training, but they knew the Scriptures and had been with Jesus. He warns that education neither disqualifies nor automatically qualifies anyone. He also links the verse to v. 12: bold claims about Christ must come with Christ's love. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Wesley: God has always had his word preached through such people, though not only through them. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/
- Henry: those who have been with Jesus should live so that others can see it. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**v. 14** Precept Austin, quoting Lenski, says the court was "checkmated." The healed man standing there was living proof of the power in Jesus' name. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Guzik: hostile examiners tested this miracle and it held up. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/

**vv. 15–17** Guzik suggests Luke may have learned what the council said in private from Saul, a later convert, if he was a member (based on Acts 26:10). He calls their admission that they "cannot deny it" proof of corrupt hearts. They admitted a miracle and still refused to submit to the God behind it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Precept Austin: they were in effect making preaching the gospel "illegal." https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Henry: an opponent's silence is sometimes almost the same as admitting the point. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**vv. 18–20** Guzik: the apostles had to speak, both because the Spirit moved them and because of Jesus' command in Acts 1:8. They were passing on what they had witnessed, not inventing it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Henry says the apostles appeal to a basic principle of natural law: when human commands clash with God's, God's commands win. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm
- Precept Austin compares their answer to Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego (Daniel 3). https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary

**vv. 21–22** Guzik: the rulers were unmoved by a miracle but moved by public opinion. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- Henry: the older the man, the harder the cure, so the grace shown is all the greater. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm
- Lowell Johnson (on Precept Austin) suggests Jesus must have passed this man many times, and he was healed later by the risen Christ for God's greater glory. https://www.preceptaustin.org/sermons-on-acts-lowell-johnson

**vv. 23–24** Gaebelein (quoted by Guzik): "with one accord" does not mean they all prayed at the same time. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- J. Vernon McGee agrees. Probably one led and the rest said amen. He notes they did not pray for the persecution to stop. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Henry explains *Despota* ("Sovereign Lord") as Master and sovereign Ruler. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**vv. 25–26** Guzik: they read their situation through Psalm 2, so they expected opposition and did not panic. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- I. Howard Marshall (via Precept Austin) says Hezekiah's prayer in Isaiah 37:16–20 also shaped this prayer. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Henry: God counts what is done against Christ as done against himself. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**v. 27** Precept Austin: the verse leaves no room for anti-Semitism, because Gentiles and Jews are all guilty. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Wesley: Jesus was anointed "to be king of Israel." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/acts/4.htm

**v. 28** See Part 2.

**vv. 29–30** A.T. Robertson (via Precept Austin): having defied the court, the apostles now pray for courage to live up to their words. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Wesley: "stretch out your hand" means putting forth your power. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/

**v. 31** Calvin: the shaking was nothing other than a sign of God's presence. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/acts/4-31.html
- Guzik: their boldness was a gift received through prayer, not something they stirred up themselves. https://enduringword.com/the-boldness-we-need/
- The Pulpit Commentary excerpt on biblehub says it was not a chance earthquake but a direct sign from God, like Pentecost. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/acts/4-31.htm
- See Part 2 on what the "filling" means.

**v. 32** Alexander Maclaren: the owners sold and handed over the money themselves. Sharing was by need, not equal shares, and there is nothing of modern communism in it. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/acts/4-32.htm
- Guzik: "Communism says, 'What is yours is mine; I'll take it.' Koinonia says, 'What is mine is yours, I'll share it.'" https://blueletterbible.org/Comm/guzik_david/StudyGuide_Act/Act_4.cfm
- Calvin finds three things praised here: unity, sharing of goods, and bold preaching of the resurrection. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/acts/4-32.html
- Precept Austin: the giving was entirely voluntary, and the text does not say everyone sold everything. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary

**v. 33** Wesley: "great grace" was a large measure of the inward power of the Holy Ghost. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/
- Guzik: the apostles' power was both the result and the root of the generosity in v. 32. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/

**vv. 34–35** Wesley sees the absence of need as proof of that grace, which must be so to the end of the world. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/
- Lowell Johnson notes they were willing to sell property and houses, not just give cash. https://www.preceptaustin.org/sermons-on-acts-lowell-johnson

**vv. 36–37** Marshall (via Precept Austin) says Luke sets Barnabas against Ananias and Sapphira in the next chapter. Precept Austin also points to Barnabas's later encouragement of John Mark. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary
- Johnson: in Acts 4 the Spirit filled Barnabas's heart; in Acts 5 Satan filled Ananias's. https://www.preceptaustin.org/sermons-on-acts-lowell-johnson
- The page's AI-generated summary of Guzik says Barnabas earned his name by generosity with both money and encouraging words. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/

## Part 2: Where Protestant traditions differ

**v. 28: God's plan and human freedom (Calvinist vs. Arminian)**
- **Gill (Calvinist Baptist):** God's decrees are eternal. Nothing happens that he has not already determined, whether he does it himself, through others, or by permitting it. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/amp/acts/4-28.html
- **Wesley (Methodist):** stresses permission. The enemies could do no more than God chose to permit, according to his plan to save mankind through his Son's sufferings. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/
- **Ellicott (Anglican):** each person's will is free and they answer for their part, yet the whole works out a larger purpose. https://biblehub.com/acts/4-28.htm
- **Pulpit Commentary:** they thought they were doing their own will but were really fulfilling God's. https://biblehub.com/acts/4-28.htm
- **Henry:** God bringing good out of their sin does not excuse it. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Act/Act_004.cfm

**vv. 8 and 31: Is this filling a second "baptism" in the Spirit?**
- **Pentecostal (Assemblies of God):** They had already been baptized in the Spirit, but under persecution they needed new power, so they prayed and were filled again. https://news.ag.org/en/article-repository/spiritual-life/2019/05/faq-baptism-in-the-holy-spirit
- **Calvary Chapel (Guzik):** believes in Spirit baptism, but says the idea that baptism is the only time a believer is filled is wrong. https://enduringword.com/blog-archive/weekly-devotionals/the-boldness-we-need/
- **Dispensational (Constable):** No tongues here; this was a fresh filling, not another baptism. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/acts/4-31.html
- **Bible.org:** Spirit baptism happens once at salvation; filling is repeated often. https://bible.org/seriespage/lesson-12-confident-witnesses-acts-41-22
- **Baptist (Piper):** reads the fillings in 4:8 and 4:31 as extraordinary power for ministry, giving bold, Christ-exalting speech. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/you-will-be-baptized-with-the-holy-spirit
- **Wesley:** filled "afresh." https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-acts-of-the-apostles/
- **Barnes:** this means confidence and boldness, not new powers as in Acts 2:4. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/acts/4-31.htm
- **An older commentator on the same page (unnamed in the excerpt):** thinks extraordinary gifts such as tongues were given again. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/acts/4-31.htm
- **The Biblical Illustrator (a collection of older sermons):** goes further, saying every worshipper received the baptism of the Spirit and was entirely sanctified. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/acts/4-31.html

**v. 32: Was it a model for holding goods in common?**
- **Wesley:** as long as that love lasted, they could not help having all things in common. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/acts-4.html
- **Chuck Smith (Calvary Chapel):** calls it a kind of communism, and says the Jerusalem church later became broke and needed Paul's collection. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/acts/4-32.html
- **Maclaren and Guzik:** deny any communism (see v. 32 above).
- **Bob Utley:** Acts cannot support communism or capitalism, since neither existed then. He warns Western readers against a capitalist bias. https://bible.org/book/export/html/21328

**v. 12: People who never hear**
- I found no tradition-by-tradition debate. Guzik says God will deal fairly with infants and those who never heard, and anyone saved is saved by Jesus' work even without full knowledge of him. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/

---

## Part 3: Other views (very limited)

- **Catholic (Haydock), v. 31:** their hearts were stirred by a new motion of grace, and the shaking resembled the Spirit's first coming. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/acts/4-31.html
- **Restoration Movement (Coffman), v. 31:** not a repeat of Pentecost but a continuation of the power promised to the Twelve. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/acts/4-31.html
- **Modern "healing services," v. 14:** Guzik contrasts this lasting, tested healing with people at some modern services who walk briefly on emotion and adrenaline and then "lost" their healing. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/acts-4/
- **NET note (quoted by Precept Austin), v. 1:** the Sadducees controlled the official political structures and were strict on law and order. https://www.preceptaustin.org/acts-4-commentary

If you'd like, a follow-up round could fill the gaps: catholic.com or newadvent.org on v. 12 and vv. 32–35, oca.org, netbible.org and bibleodyssey.org, the Ellicott and Gill pages on biblehub for each verse, and any prosperity-gospel use of v. 34.
